results.question: How many employees are there?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as employee_count FROM employees;

results.question: How many projects have status 'active'?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as active_projects FROM projects WHERE status = 'active'

results.question: List the names of all clients in Denmark in alphabetical order.
results.sql: SELECT name FROM clients WHERE country = 'Denmark' ORDER BY name ASC;

results.question: What is the total budget across all projects?
results.sql: SELECT SUM(budget) as total_budget FROM projects;

results.question: How many invoices are overdue?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as overdue_invoices FROM invoices WHERE status = 'overdue'

results.question: How many expenses are in the Travel category?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as travel_expense_count FROM expenses WHERE category = 'Travel'

results.question: How many employees work in each office?
results.sql: SELECT office, COUNT(*) as employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY office ORDER BY office

results.question: What is the largest single expense amount?
results.sql: SELECT MAX(amount) as largest_expense FROM expenses

results.question: Which client has the highest total project budget? Give the client name.
results.sql:
SELECT c.name
FROM clients c
JOIN projects p ON c.id = p.client_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY SUM(p.budget) DESC
LIMIT 1

results.question: What is the total invoiced amount per client, highest first? Include every client that has been invoiced.
results.sql:
SELECT 
  c.name as client,
  SUM(i.amount) as total_invoiced
FROM invoices i
JOIN projects p ON i.project_id = p.id
JOIN clients c ON p.client_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_invoiced DESC

results.question: How many hours have been logged in total on project 1?
results.sql: SELECT SUM(hours) as total_hours FROM timesheets WHERE project_id = 1

results.question: Which 5 employees have logged the most billable hours? Give their names and the hours.
results.sql:
SELECT 
    e.name,
    SUM(t.hours) as total_billable_hours
FROM timesheets t
JOIN employees e ON t.employee_id = e.id
WHERE t.billable = 1
GROUP BY t.employee_id, e.name
ORDER BY total_billable_hours DESC
LIMIT 5

results.question: What is the total amount of expenses per category?
results.sql:
SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total_amount
FROM expenses
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category

results.question: Which employees lead more than 3 projects? Give their names.
results.sql:
SELECT e.name
FROM employees e
WHERE e.id IN (
    SELECT lead_id
    FROM projects
    GROUP BY lead_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 3
)

results.question: What is the average amount of the paid invoices?
results.sql: SELECT AVG(amount) as average_paid_invoice_amount FROM invoices WHERE status = 'paid'

results.question: Which clients have no overdue invoices? Give the client names.
results.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT c.name
FROM clients c
WHERE c.id NOT IN (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.client_id
  FROM projects p
  INNER JOIN invoices i ON p.id = i.project_id
  WHERE i.status = 'overdue'
)
ORDER BY c.name

results.question: How many different employees have logged time on active projects?
results.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t.employee_id)
FROM timesheets t
JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id
WHERE p.status = 'active'

results.question: What is the total unpaid invoice amount (invoices that are not paid) per client country?
results.sql:
SELECT 
    c.country,
    SUM(i.amount) as total_unpaid_amount
FROM invoices i
JOIN projects p ON i.project_id = p.id
JOIN clients c ON p.client_id = c.id
WHERE i.status != 'paid'
GROUP BY c.country
ORDER BY total_unpaid_amount DESC

results.question: Which projects have been invoiced for more than their budget? Give the project name, total invoiced and budget.
results.sql:
SELECT 
  p.name as project_name,
  SUM(i.amount) as total_invoiced,
  p.budget
FROM projects p
JOIN invoices i ON p.id = i.project_id
GROUP BY p.id, p.name, p.budget
HAVING SUM(i.amount) > p.budget
ORDER BY p.name

results.question: How many invoices were issued in each year?
results.sql:
SELECT 
    strftime('%Y', issue_date) AS year,
    COUNT(*) AS invoice_count
FROM invoices
GROUP BY strftime('%Y', issue_date)
ORDER BY year;

results.question: Which employee logged the most hours in March 2026? Give the name.
results.sql:
SELECT e.name, SUM(t.hours) as total_hours
FROM timesheets t
JOIN employees e ON t.employee_id = e.id
WHERE t.work_date >= '2026-03-01' AND t.work_date < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY t.employee_id, e.name
ORDER BY total_hours DESC
LIMIT 1

results.question: What percentage of all logged hours are billable? Round to 1 decimal place.
results.sql:
SELECT 
  ROUND(
    (SUM(CASE WHEN billable = 1 THEN hours ELSE 0 END) / SUM(hours)) * 100.0,
    1
  ) AS billable_percentage
FROM timesheets

results.question: On average, how many days pass between the issue date and the paid date of paid invoices? Round to 1 decimal place.
results.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(issue_date)), 1) as avg_days_to_payment
FROM invoices
WHERE status = 'paid' AND paid_date IS NOT NULL

results.question: Which clients have at least one overdue invoice? Give the client names.
results.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT c.name
FROM clients c
JOIN projects p ON c.id = p.client_id
JOIN invoices i ON p.id = i.project_id
WHERE i.status = 'overdue'
ORDER BY c.name;

results.question: For each project lead, what is the combined budget of the projects they lead? Show the top 3 leads by name.
results.sql:
SELECT 
  e.name,
  SUM(p.budget) AS combined_budget
FROM projects p
JOIN employees e ON p.lead_id = e.id
GROUP BY p.lead_id, e.name
ORDER BY combined_budget DESC
LIMIT 3

results.question: Which employee has the highest total expenses? Give the name and the total.
results.sql:
SELECT e.name, SUM(ex.amount) as total_expenses
FROM employees e
JOIN expenses ex ON e.id = ex.employee_id
GROUP BY e.id, e.name
ORDER BY total_expenses DESC
LIMIT 1

results.question: Which month had the highest total invoiced amount? Give the month as YYYY-MM and the total.
results.sql:
SELECT 
  strftime('%Y-%m', issue_date) AS month,
  SUM(amount) AS total_invoiced
FROM invoices
GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', issue_date)
ORDER BY total_invoiced DESC
LIMIT 1;

results.question: How many projects have both an overdue invoice and an expense above 4000?
results.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id)
FROM projects p
WHERE p.id IN (
    SELECT project_id FROM invoices WHERE status = 'overdue'
)
AND p.id IN (
    SELECT project_id FROM expenses WHERE amount > 4000
)
